title: Cannabis Chocolate Tarts with Cherry (Gluten-Free)
h1: Gluten-Free Chocolate Cherry Tarts, Infused Three Ways
metaDescription: Mini buckwheat-crust chocolate tarts with a cherry glaze, three places to add your infusion (crust, ganache or topping) and simple per-tart dose math.
excerpt: Make-ahead mini chocolate tarts on a buckwheat crust with a tart cherry glaze. Infuse the crust, the ganache or the topping, then total the mg and divide.
keyTakeaways: You can infuse the crust butter, the ganache or the whipped topping; start with just one.
Add up the THC from every infused layer, then divide by the number of tarts or wedges.
Buckwheat is naturally gluten-free, but flour can pick up gluten from shared equipment, so check labels.
Keep the tarts covered, labeled and refrigerated, and eat them within about three days.
body:
This cannabis chocolate tart recipe makes six make-ahead minis: a cocoa-buckwheat crust, silky dark chocolate ganache, a tart cherry glaze and a spoonful of mascarpone cream. It's a gluten-free cannabis dessert, and you decide where the dose lives.

## Dosing a cannabis chocolate tart: pick your infusion point

| Infusion point | How to add it | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| Crust | Swap part of the cold butter for cold cannabutter | Bakes about 15 minutes |
| Ganache | Stir melted cannabutter into the hot cream | Easiest to mix evenly |
| Topping | Whip infused cream with the mascarpone | Needs equal spoonfuls |

Start with one point; an infused ganache mixes most evenly. Infusing more than one layer? Add the totals. With cannabutter at about 30 mg per tablespoon, 1 tablespoon in the ganache gives about 5 mg per tart. Add the same to the crust and each tart reaches about 10 mg, the most a licensed adult-use edible may hold per serving in Michigan.

Have half a tart first and wait 2 hours, since effects can take that long to show. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) explains starting amounts.

## Ingredients and method

The buckwheat tart crust is buckwheat flour, cornstarch, cocoa, sugar and salt rubbed with cold butter, then bound with vanilla and a splash of cold water or cherry juice. With no gluten to hold it together, press it into the pans by hand instead of rolling. Chill, bake at 350°F and cool. Baking for someone who avoids gluten? Choose flours labeled gluten-free and check the cocoa and chocolate too.

For the ganache, pour steaming cream over chopped dark chocolate, wait a minute and whisk until glossy, then fill the shells and chill. Simmer tart cherry juice with sugar into a syrup, and whip cream with mascarpone to soft peaks. Our [cannabutter recipe](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/) covers the infusion, and our budtenders can help you choose flower at [your nearest store](/dispensary-locations/).

## Serving

Top each tart with a drizzle of cherry syrup, one spoonful of topping and fresh cherries or berries. If the whipped cream is infused, use the same spoon for every tart.

## Storage and labeling

Cover the tarts, mark the container with the date and estimated mg per tart, and refrigerate it away from plain desserts. They're freshest within about three days. Keep them on a shelf kids and pets can't reach, and after an accidental bite, call poison control at 1-800-222-1222.

## Dairy-free version

Use stick-style plant butter in the crust and canna-coconut oil as the infusion. Make the ganache with warm full-fat coconut cream and dairy-free chocolate, and whip chilled coconut cream for the topping. Find more ideas in our [infused recipes](/blog/recipes/).

These tarts are for adults 21 and older who know they're infused.

faq.q: How do I make infused cream?
faq.a: For ganache, stir a measured spoonful of melted cannabutter into the warm cream. For whipping, steep decarbed flower in heavy cream over very low heat for about an hour without letting it boil, strain it, and chill it overnight. Label infused cream and use it within a couple of days.

Yes, naturally; despite its name, buckwheat isn't wheat. The catch is cross-contact: gluten can get in when it's harvested or processed on equipment shared with wheat. Celiac groups suggest products labeled or tested gluten-free, and no bulk bins. Baking for someone with celiac disease? Check every ingredient, not just the flour.

faq.q: Can I make one large tart instead?
faq.a: Yes. Press the crust into a 9-inch tart pan and bake it for 20 to 25 minutes, until it looks dry and smells toasty. Fill and chill as usual, mark 8 equal wedges before cutting, and divide the total mg by 8 instead of 6.

ingredients: 1/4 cup sugar, plus 3 tablespoons for the glaze
1/2 cup (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cubed (swap cold cannabutter in for part of it to infuse the crust)
2 to 4 tablespoons cold water or cherry juice
8 ounces dark chocolate (60 to 70%), finely chopped
1 cup heavy cream, for the ganache
Melted cannabutter for the ganache, measured to your dose (optional)
1 cup tart cherry juice, for the glaze
1/2 cup cold heavy cream (or chilled infused cream), for the topping
Fresh cherries and berries, for serving
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour, cornstarch, cocoa, 1/4 cup sugar and salt. Rub in the cold butter (and any cannabutter) with your fingertips until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.

Stir in the vanilla and just enough cold water or juice for the crumbs to hold when squeezed. Divide evenly among six 4-inch tart pans, press into the bottoms and sides, prick with a fork and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Bake the shells for 15 to 18 minutes, until firm and fragrant, then cool completely.

Heat 1 cup cream until steaming and stir in any measured cannabutter. Pour it over the chopped chocolate, wait 1 minute and whisk until smooth. Divide evenly among the shells and chill until set, at least 2 hours.
Simmer the cherry juice with 3 tablespoons sugar for 15 to 20 minutes, until it reduces to about 1/3 cup. It thickens as it cools.
Whip the cold cream, mascarpone and powdered sugar to soft peaks.
To serve, drizzle each tart with cherry syrup, add one equal spoonful of topping and finish with fresh fruit.
recipe.dosingNote: Read these numbers as estimates. Example: 1 tablespoon of cannabutter at about 30 mg in the ganache gives 30 ÷ 6 tarts ≈ 5 mg per tart at most. Infuse the crust the same way and it's about 10 mg per tart. Actual THC per tart depends on your flower's potency and on what decarboxylation and infusion lost along the way. Start with half a tart and wait at least 2 hours before having more. Label the tarts as infused, and keep them away from children and pets.

review.summary: 19 claims checked: 18 ok, 1 fixed (0 wrong, 0 unsupported, 1 overstated). The buckwheat FAQ no longer says it is 'often grown, milled or packed near wheat'; it now names the shared harvesting and processing equipment the Celiac Disease Foundation describes.

claims.claim: Dose math: 1 tablespoon of cannabutter at about 30 mg in the ganache / 6 tarts = about 5 mg per tart; crust infused the same way = about 10 mg; one 9-inch tart / 8 wedges
claims.source: arithmetic on an example potency the text labels as an example (30 / 6 = 5; 60 / 6 = 10)

claims.claim: About 10 mg is the most a licensed adult-use edible may hold per serving in Michigan
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-thc-limits: 'Adult-use edibles in Michigan are capped at 10 mg THC per dose and 200 mg per package' (CRA technical bulletin, April 24, 2025; law-facts source, not refetched)

claims.claim: Effects can take up to 2 hours to show; have half a tart first and wait (at least) 2 hours
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/poisoning.html (WebFetch): 'Take from 30 minutes to 2 hours to feel intoxicating effects.'

claims.claim: Keep the tarts where kids and pets can't reach; after an accidental bite call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/poisoning.html: 'your local or regional poison control center at 1-800-222-1222'; 'out of the reach and sight of children and pets'

claims.claim: Buckwheat is naturally gluten-free (title, takeaway, FAQ)
claims.source: https://celiac.org/gluten-free-living/gluten-free-foods/ (WebFetch): 'Buckwheat groats (also known as kasha)' listed under naturally gluten-free foods

claims.claim: Despite its name, buckwheat isn't wheat (FAQ)
claims.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26270637/ (Giménez-Bastida & Zieliński 2015, abstract via E-utilities): 'Buckwheat (BW) is a gluten-free pseudocereal that belongs to the Polygonaceae family' (wheat is a grass)

claims.claim: Buckwheat flour can pick up gluten from shared equipment, so check labels (takeaway)
claims.source: https://celiac.org/gluten-free-living/gluten-free-foods/: 'some naturally gluten-free grains may contain gluten from cross-contact with gluten-containing grains'; oats 'harvested and processed with the same equipment that is used for wheat'; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20497786/ (Thompson 2010): 7 of 22 unlabeled inherently gluten-free grains, seeds and flours had mean gluten >= 20 ppm

claims.claim: FAQ: cross-contact happens 'since it's often grown, milled or packed near wheat'
claims.fix: now 'gluten can get in when it's harvested or processed on equipment shared with wheat': the sources name shared harvesting and processing equipment, not neighboring fields, and give no frequency for buckwheat
claims.source: https://celiac.org/gluten-free-living/gluten-free-foods/ (cross-contact during harvesting and processing; shared equipment); https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20497786/ (a 22-sample pilot, not a buckwheat-specific rate)

claims.claim: Celiac groups suggest products labeled or tested gluten-free, and no bulk bins (FAQ)
claims.source: https://celiac.org/gluten-free-living/gluten-free-foods/: 'It is not recommended to purchase grains from bulk bins because of the possibility of cross-contact with gluten.'; 'purchase only versions that are tested for the presence of gluten and contain less than 20 parts per million'

claims.claim: Tarts are freshest within about three days; takeaway: eat them within about three days
claims.source: https://extension.illinois.edu/food-safety/leftovers (WebFetch): 'Use refrigerated leftover food within 3-4 days.' (three days sits inside that window)

claims.claim: Label infused cream and use it within a couple of days (FAQ)
claims.source: conservative, inside the 3-4 day refrigerated window on https://extension.illinois.edu/food-safety/leftovers

claims.claim: Bake the press-in shells at 350°F: 15 to 18 minutes for 4-inch minis (table: about 15), 20 to 25 minutes for a 9-inch tart
claims.source: https://edibleeastbay.com/2016/08/12/elderberry-buckwheat-tart/ (WebFetch): press-in buckwheat crust in 'an 8-inch or 9-inch tart pan', '350°', 'for 15 minutes', 'until golden-brown'; https://jernejkitchen.com/recipes/bread-and-doughs/gluten-free-buckwheat-tart-crust: 9-inch buckwheat-cacao shell at '175 °C / 350 °F', 20 minutes with weights plus 15

claims.claim: Simmer 1 cup tart cherry juice with sugar 15 to 20 minutes, to about 1/3 cup; it thickens as it cools
claims.source: https://www.babaganosh.org/wprm_print/11664 (WebFetch): tart cherry juice and sugar, 'let simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes', 'until the syrup coats a spoon or spatula'

claims.claim: Ganache: pour steaming cream over chopped dark chocolate, wait a minute, whisk; an infused ganache mixes most evenly
claims.source: standard ganache technique; the evenness point is reasoning (a whisked liquid emulsion spreads an infusion more evenly than a crumb crust or a whipped topping)

claims.claim: Infused cream: steep decarbed flower in heavy cream over very low heat about an hour without boiling, strain, chill overnight, then whip
claims.source: method description, no figure from a source; heated and re-chilled heavy cream still whips, and the text keeps the dose math to measured cannabutter

claims.claim: Actual THC per tart depends on the flower's potency and on decarboxylation and infusion losses (dosing note)
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC): 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

review.notes: Independent fact-check: Celiac Disease Foundation and CDC pages opened with WebFetch; Giménez-Bastida 2015, Thompson 2010 and Wang 2016 read through NCBI E-utilities or Europe PMC; Illinois Extension (leftovers) and three recipe pages opened for times. Michigan's 10 mg per-serving cap checked against facts/law-facts.json mi-thc-limits (CRA bulletin of April 24, 2025, verified by the law refuter and not refetched). Beyond Celiac and foodsafety.gov refuse automated fetches (403), so neither is cited. High Society appears once: budtenders help you choose flower, with the store locator link. Writer's notes: No celiac-safe claim: the article says buckwheat is naturally gluten-free and tells readers baking for someone with celiac disease to check every ingredient. No brand. High Society appears once (budtenders help choose flower: hs-facts services.inStoreVisit; store locator link). FAQ idea "best place to add cannabis" is answered by the dosing section and its table.
